customManagers.description: The platform bundle version each cluster pins (ADR-064). Matched under the chart source only: a cluster's bundle.yaml carries a second targetRevision naming the branch this repository's values are read from, and rewriting that one would repoint the repository at a chart version and stop the cluster resolving its own values. The match spans targetRevision AND the bundleVersion parameter so a promotion moves both together -- the chart is told which version it is, and a chart that is told the wrong one sources its boundaries from the platform's git repository instead of the distribution it was published in.
customManagers.autoReplaceStringTemplate:
chart: environment-manager
      targetRevision: {{{newValue}}}
      helm:
        parameters:
          - name: bundleVersion
            value: "{{{newValue}}}"

packageRules.description: Production clusters are proposed but never merged automatically. A version reaches production because someone decided it should, which is the decision ADR-065 reserves to the tenant and the one an automatic merge would take on its behalf.

prBodyNotes: This proposal changes the platform bundle version this cluster pins. It carries none of the bundle's content: the chart is pulled from the registry at the version below.
Nothing is applied by the platform. This cluster changes when this pull request is merged and this repository's own control plane reconciles the result.

What the version spans -- the versions crossed since the one in use, any security fixes among them, whether each step is reversible, and the minimum version it may be taken from -- is recorded in the release notes linked above.

Closing this pull request declines the upgrade. Declining is not a breach of support; support follows the version, and a version outside its supported window is one the platform stops promising maintenance for rather than one it forces.
